memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From the Desert of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon offering peace and saying, "Let us pass through your country. We will stay on the main road; we will not turn aside to the right or to the left. Sell us food to eat and water to drink for their price in silver. Only let us pass through on foot—as the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, and the Moabites, who live in Ar, did for us—until we cross the Jordan into the land the Lord our God is giving us." - Deut 2:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before any battle, Moses sent messengers to Sihon with a genuine offer of peace. Israel asked only to pass through on the main road, promising to pay for food and water and to cause no trouble. Even though God had promised them victory over Sihon, they still extended a sincere offer of peace first. They did not rush to war; they sought the path of peace where it was possible.

This is a beautiful example of God's people seeking peace even when they had the promise of victory. Israel could have simply attacked, confident in God's word. Instead, they first offered peaceful passage, honest dealing, and fair payment. There is a graciousness here that reflects the character God desires in His people.

The New Testament calls believers to this same peaceable spirit. Paul writes, "If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone" (Rom 12:18). We are to be peacemakers, seeking reconciliation and offering goodwill wherever we can. Even when we are in the right, even when we have confidence in God's backing, we are not to be quick to conflict but eager for peace.

Of course, peace is not always possible, and Sihon would refuse this offer. But that would be his choice, not Israel's failure to seek peace. Our responsibility is to do all we can, as far as it depends on us, to pursue peace. This reflects the heart of Christ, the Prince of Peace, who came to reconcile us to God and calls His followers blessed when they make peace (Matt 5:9). Wherever you can, choose the path of peace and honest dealing, leaving the outcome in God's hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you seek peace with others, even when you feel you are in the right?
2. How can you be a peacemaker in a current conflict or tension?
3. How does Christ, the Prince of Peace, shape the way you deal with others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Prince of Peace, thank You for reconciling me to God. Make me a peacemaker who seeks peace and honest dealing wherever possible, leaving outcomes in Your hands and reflecting Your gracious heart. Amen.
